source.title: Minimum Number of Coins to be Added

teaching.hint: What is the first sum you cannot yet make, and how large can the next useful coin be?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: If all sums below a frontier are covered, a coin no larger than the frontier extends the covered interval; a larger coin leaves the frontier missing.
solution_outline.approach: Process original coins in ascending order. Keep the first uncovered positive sum. Consume each available coin that bridges it; otherwise add a coin equal to that missing sum, then continue.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before each step, every positive value below `missing` is obtainable, and the unused original coins are no smaller than the next one under consideration.
solution_outline.correctness: When the next coin exceeds `missing`, no original coin can fill the gap, so an addition is forced. Adding exactly `missing` gives the largest possible new covered interval among legal additions, preserving an optimal plan.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n log n) time for sorting and O(1) auxiliary space beyond sorting for n coins; use a wide integer for the frontier.
solution_outline.pitfall: Using an original coin larger than the first gap does not make that gap obtainable.

common_wrong_turns: Advance past a coin that is still too large
source_fidelity_notes: Clarifies occurrence reuse and that added coin values are unrestricted positive integers; the original subsequence wording was shortened.
